item.text: {"searches":[{"reason":"Develop practical GRU4Rec probes for current intent: remove recent versus older events, shuffle valid history positions, and truncate prefixes while preserving left padding and final-nonpadding readout. Measure changes in held-out training-prefix target ranks and recurrent states, stratified by history length and recency. This should distinguish ignored recent evidence, excessive dependence on the last item, and harmful persistence of older interests without accessing test data.","query":"GRU4Rec sequential recommendation temporal counterfactual diagnostics recent intent history deletion order permutation hidden state sensitivity 2024 2025 2026"},{"reason":"Connect qualitative rejection reasons to measurable evidence using only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Investigate locally fitted text representations and evidence-grounded annotation that separate recent-intent support, possible functional redundancy, and insufficient information. Calibrate proxies against available explicit feedback, report uncertainty and coverage, and avoid claiming observed compatibility, ownership needs, mood, or simulator traits from weak textual clues.","query":"recommendation diagnostic evaluation qualitative user feedback current intent redundancy evidence grounded text proxies abstention calibration 2024 2025 2026"},{"reason":"Replace scale-sensitive pairwise margins and raw embedding cosine averages with a trustworthy diagnostic suite: frequency-stratified target ranks, hard-negative stress tests, effective representation rank, and GRU gradient or state-retention measurements. Compare sampled-candidate and full-catalog unseen-item rankings on permitted training-prefix targets, with user-level uncertainty, while leaving pinned validation evaluation unchanged. Seek evidence that each probe identifies a specific training or recurrent-network failure rather than merely correlating with popularity.","query":"sequential recommender diagnostic probes sampled evaluation full catalog ranking popularity bias effective rank recurrent gradient validation negative controls 2024 2025 2026"}]}
